title: Additive profile-merge strategy and annotated audit export for compact changelogs
author: Clara Nguyen
release_notes: Introduce additive/annotated profile-merge algorithm to reduce churn in model variants; add an export endpoint that produces compact, audit-backed changelog bundles for release automation.
description:
Context and motivation: The model registry has accumulated many near-duplicate variant profiles when teams publish small, orthogonal tweaks (tokenization hints, quantization preference, or perf heuristics). This PR introduces an additive profile-merge strategy (opt-in) that reduces duplicate profiles by merging non-conflicting deltas and emitting an annotated audit trail so downstream consumers (release assembler, documentation generator, on-board pipelines) can reconstruct the origin and reason for each merged change.

Goals: 1) Reduce profile explosion for minor deltas without losing provenance. 2) Provide a compact changelog export that is machine-consumable for release automation. 3) Preserve determinism and reversibility (ability to unmerge via explicit rollback entries).

What this PR contains (single continuous description): Implement additive profile-merge engine under src/merging/additive_merge.py with a deterministic key ordering and conflict resolution rules; introduce profile-audit-log model and an export handler at api/exports/annotated_changelog.py that generates compressed, signed bundles (ndjson + minimal manifest); wire a feature flag (FEATURE_PROFILE_MERGE) to registry config and a migration utility that can roll up existing near-duplicates into a merged-profile set; add unit and integration tests and update documentation and CLI hints.

High-level checklist (what reviewers should validate): - Design doc summary included in PR description and linked Linear tasks. - Deterministic merge ordering and conflict resolution rules implemented and covered by tests. - Audit entries include: author, original_profile_id, delta_patch (JSON patch), timestamp, Linear ticket (if present), and merge_reason tag. - Exported changelog bundles validate against a compact schema and can be consumed by the release assembler with a simple --apply flag. - No silent data loss: rollback path created via audit log reverse-apply. - Performance: merging pass on 10k small profiles completes under 30s in CI-ish environment (see perf test output).

Commit summary: - 7 commits total (squashed on merge). 1) add additive merge algorithm and unit tests 2) add profile audit log model and persistence hooks 3) add annotated changelog export API + docs 4) add migration script and CLI command 5) add integration tests and perf test harness 6) docs: registry/merge.md and examples 7) minor fixes from review feedback (schema validation, edge-case assert).

Files touched (high level): - src/merging/additive_merge.py (core algorithm) - src/models/profile_audit.py (audit model + serializer) - api/exports/annotated_changelog.py (HTTP handler + CLI export) - tools/migrations/merge_duplicates.py (one-off migrator) - tests/unit/test_additive_merge.py - tests/integration/test_annotated_export.py - docs/registry/merge.md - cli/registry.py (new `registry merge-compact` command) - infra/feature_flags.yaml (feature gating)

Small illustrative snippet (from additive_merge merge strategy):

# pseudo
for key in sorted(delta_keys):
    if key in base and is_nonconflicting(base[key], delta[key]):
        base[key] = merge_values(base[key], delta[key])  # additive union for lists, max for ints
    else:
        mark_conflict(profile_id, key)
"""

Review conversation highlights: - Ethan Patel: "We need to ensure the audit entries are immutable and signed; otherwise downstream consumers can't trust merges." Author reply: "Added a signature field (HMAC with registry key) and included verification in export handler; tests added." - Maya Rios: "What happens when two merges occur concurrently?" Author reply: "Merges are scoped by profile namespace + monotonic merge-seq; we acquire a lightweight per-namespace lock in the store. Added a contention test that simulates concurrent merges." - Noah Kim: "Edge-case: quantization pref conflicts with kernel hints — which wins?" Author reply: "We treat model-safety fields (quantization_precision) as high-priority and require explicit override to merge; documented in merge.md." - Reviewers requested better logging for migration; added verbose --dry-run mode to the migration tool.

CI summary: - Unit tests: pass - Integration tests: pass (including perf harness run) - Lint: pass - Type check: pass - Release checks: pass. Note: a transient flake occurred in integration on first run (DB connection timeout); rerun fixed it.

Performance notes: - Perf harness (tests/integration/perf_merge.py) runs a simulated dataset of 10k profiles with average 3-field deltas; merge completes in ~22s on CI runner (8 CPU). Memory peak ~420MB. This meets the perf target in ENG-2345.

Migration guidance: - New opt-in feature flag FEATURE_PROFILE_MERGE=false by default. - To adopt for an org: run `tools/migrations/merge_duplicates.py --org <org> --dry-run` to preview candidates. Review the generated annotated export (ndjson) and then run without --dry-run to apply. Exports are saved to /var/tmp/registry_exports/<org>/timestamp and include a manifest.json with signatures and a concise changelog body for release notes automation.

Backward compatibility and safety: - Existing profile IDs remain stable; merged profiles are assigned a new canonical id with a pointer to previous ids via audit entries. - Consumers that rely on exact profile ids will see a deprecation warning in read endpoints for a configurable period; read-only aliases remain until the rollback window (configurable).

Security & privacy: - Audit export bundles are signed and optionally encrypted via KMS key. The export handler respects customer-level redaction preferences when flagged on a profile.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main on 2025-11-01 by Maya Rios. The final commit message references ENG-2345 and SUP-712 and includes a short summary and migration instructions.

Follow-ups tracked: - ENG-2499: Add UI for reviewing merge candidates in Console (depends on export manifest). - ENG-2567: Add auto-suggestion engine to propose merge_grouping thresholds per org.

Notes for release notes automation: The annotated export schema includes a `changelog_compact` entry that the release assembler will convert to a human-friendly blurb. This PR adds a mapping rule in the assembler that collapses low-impact merges into a single bullet to reduce noise in release notes.

Why this is different from previous work: Many earlier PRs focused on generating changelogs or tagging provenance after the fact. This change takes a proactive approach: reduce profile fragmentation by merging additive deltas while preserving a rich, machine-readable audit trail so nothing is lost and automation can continue operating on a compact representation.
